clue.text: Am I going to reveal information about live opera?

blocks.note: the question recast as 'Will I?'
to live is to be, as in 'I am'
to tell is to give information about something

explanation.surface: Someone nervously wonders whether to leak details about a live opera performance.
explanation.walkthrough: WILL I + AM + TELL gives WILLIAM TELL; the question itself sounds like the rapper will.i.am about to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini's final opera, famous for its overture, is named after the Swiss archer hero.

clue.text: Wife husband’s left harassed and offended

indicators.note: the husband has gone away, so his letter departs from the next word

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
H is the abbreviation for husband
to hound someone is to harass them

explanation.surface: A wife, abandoned by her husband and pestered, feels hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as the husband walking out, which fits the surface; cryptically it removes his letter from the harassment word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose feelings are hurt is described as wounded, an emotional sense of being injured.

clue.text: Compare president with Lincoln, utterly heartless about it

indicators.note: with the whole interior cut away only the two outermost letters of the name survive
the surviving letters wrap themselves around the other piece mentioned

blocks.note: just the first and last letters
Ike was the nickname of US president Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A historian sets one president beside Abraham Lincoln and finds the newcomer callous.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to compare them, pointing out a similarity.

clue.text: The writer’s shame, concealing base wickedness

indicators.note: something concealed is hidden inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the writer is 'I', so the writer's is I'M (I am)
as in 'what a shame' = 'what a pity'
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: An author confesses to shame at hiding some vile wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: I'M + PI(E)TY: the mathematical constant e is the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: Impiety is lack of reverence for God, a form of sinfulness or wickedness.

clue.text: Transport home welcomed by Mike and Jack

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by hosts is taken in among them

blocks.note: a mike or mic is a microphone
at home means in
a jack (tar) is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman); 'and' simply adds it on

explanation.surface: Two men named Mike and Jack give someone a lift home.
explanation.walkthrough: The home piece goes in right after the first letter. A minicab is a British private-hire taxi booked by phone; Jack Tar is old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A minicab is a hired car, so it serves as a means of transport for passengers.

clue.text: Cryptic clue by one academic using traditional maths

indicators.note: a cryptic version of something is puzzling and garbled, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the four letters to be rearranged
Roman numeral one
a dean is a senior university academic

explanation.surface: A don writes a puzzling clue built on old-fashioned mathematics.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclidean geometry follows the ancient Greek Euclid's classical axioms, the conventional school mathematics of plane figures.

clue.text: Piece of rope left on an overturned cart

indicators.note: a vehicle that has turned over now faces the other way, so its name is read backwards

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
a dray is a heavy cart, traditionally for beer barrels

explanation.surface: A bit of rope is abandoned on a cart that has tipped over.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a short cord or line, used on ships for fastening or around the neck for a whistle.

clue.text: Unpleasantly posh food in meal reduced by half

indicators.note: cutting a word to half its length throws away its second half
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: supper is an evening meal
tuck is British slang for food, especially snacks at school

explanation.surface: A snobbish diner complains that the meal served was only half portions.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is British school slang for snacks and sweets, as in a tuck shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuck-up person is snobbishly superior, thinking themselves above others in an off-putting way.

clue.text: Voyager undertook this small step before many steps

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a pace is a step
a flight of stairs is a series of steps

explanation.surface: An echo of Armstrong's 'small step', with Voyager making a giant leap after it.
explanation.walkthrough: Voyager is the NASA probe now in interstellar space; the surface plays on Armstrong's 'one small step'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Voyager probes travelled beyond the solar system, a mission through outer space.

clue.text: It’s impossible, note, to invest in new food e-tailer

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so this letter goes inside

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
Ocado is a British online grocery retailer
N is short for note

explanation.surface: Someone is told no when proposing a stake in an online grocery start-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Ocado is a British online supermarket delivering groceries; the note letter goes inside it after the new letter is placed in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The pidgin-style phrase is an informal refusal meaning that something cannot be done.

clue.text: Test this funky old track in record we hear

indicators.note: funky suggests something odd and jumbled, so the preceding word's letters are mixed up

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken examination
the four letters to be rearranged
O is the abbreviation for old
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A DJ plays an old funk track to check a vinyl recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funky old track' reads as music, but funky only scrambles 'this' and the track is a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral history is a historical account gathered by recording people's spoken memories, so it is heard rather than read.

clue.text: Nearly burning forest in play

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: ardent means burning, fiery

explanation.surface: A forest is almost on fire during a stage performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forest of Arden is the woodland setting for much of Shakespeare's As You Like It.

clue.text: Awfully nice, saving character dropped in EastEnders car fare

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the next word's letters are disordered
to save something is to keep it safe within, so a letter is held inside

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
Cockney Londoners, as in the TV soap EastEnders, drop the letter aitch
Lada is a Russian car make

explanation.surface: A very nice character written out of the soap EastEnders had been saving for a car.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in East London, where Cockney speech drops the H. 'Character' looks like a person in the soap; it is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican tortilla dish, and fare means food served to eat.

clue.text: Knocking on wood, extremely lucky

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those are kept

blocks.note: elder is a tree, so its wood
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone touches wood for very good luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking on wood' reads as one superstitious phrase, but the definition stops at 'Knocking on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking on is informal British for getting old, as in 'knocking on a bit', meaning aged.

clue.text: Items sold in sweet shop and bakery around northern province of The King?

indicators.note: the two items surround the next letter, sitting on either side of it

blocks.note: rock is a hard stick of candy sold at British seaside resorts
a bread roll, sold at a bakery
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A sweet shop and bakery stand near some northern region belonging to a king.
explanation.walkthrough: The King is Elvis Presley, crowned King of the genre; the 'province' is his musical realm, not a territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis is crowned the King of rock 'n' roll, so that music genre is his realm or domain.

clue.text: Inspiration to adopt Democrat’s liberal attitude

indicators.note: adopting someone takes them into the family, so a letter is taken inside

blocks.note: inspiration in its literal sense is drawing in breath
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A source of inspiration is taking up a Democrat's open-minded outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiration' looks figurative but is used in its physical sense of breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth of mind or outlook means tolerance and broad sympathies, a liberal way of thinking.

clue.text: Reasonable person who serves in pub

indicators.note: one thing inside another, so the first piece goes within the second

blocks.note: your local is the nearby pub you usually drink in
a GI is an American soldier, someone serving in the army

explanation.surface: The bartender at the pub is a sensible sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person who serves in pub' suggests a barman, but the serving is military: LO(GI)CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical means sensible and following sound reasoning, just as reasonable does.

clue.text: Good parrot cages provided, getting praise

indicators.note: a creature that cages something shuts it inside

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a lory is a small brightly coloured parrot
provided (that) means if

explanation.surface: A well-behaved parrot kept in a cage earns compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: The parrot is caging, not caged: G + LOR(IF)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To glorify is to extol or worship someone, heaping lavish acclaim on them.

clue.text: Time to forego pleasures? I try, in a dark patch

blocks.note: Lent is the Christian season of self-denial before Easter
taken as written
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Someone gives up treats for a while and tries hard during a gloomy spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark patch' reads as a bad period of life, but it is a mark on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A lentigo is a small brown spot on the skin, such as a freckle or age spot.

clue.text: Flogs paper at first showing what beach bodies have?

indicators.note: the second item named is to be placed at the start, ahead of the first

blocks.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
to tan someone's hide is to beat or flog them

explanation.surface: A vendor sells a newspaper first, as a teaser for its photos of sunbathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogs paper' suggests selling newspapers; flogs means beats here. The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunbathers on the beach acquire browned skin from exposure to sunlight.

clue.text: Taking off Asian dress, caught holding the thing up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top
something held is kept inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a sari is a draped garment worn in South Asia
it means the thing
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone removing a sari is spotted while lifting something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' seems to mean undressing but means mimicking: SA(TI)RI + C.
explanation.definitionFit: A take-off is a mocking imitation, so satirical writing is engaged in taking off its targets.

clue.text: Like to keep running miles, wanting direction

indicators.note: running can mean in disorder, the letters set moving out of place
to keep something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: as means like, in the manner of
the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A jogger keeps clocking miles without knowing which way to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimless means lacking purpose or goal, and wanting here means lacking.

clue.text: Gillingham’s number one fan imbibing drinks and snack

indicators.note: number one in the town's name is its first letter
imbibing means drinking in, so the drinks go inside

blocks.note: first letter
a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
a nut is an enthusiast, as in a football nut

explanation.surface: Gillingham football club's top supporter has drinks and a bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Gillingham is a Kent town with a football club; 'number one fan' looks like a single phrase, but number one only selects a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundnut is a peanut, a common snack food eaten salted or roasted.

clue.text: Musicians carefully inspect disc

blocks.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
O is round like a disc

explanation.surface: A band's members check a record closely.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small jazz or dance band, a group of performing players.

clue.text: Pole in Scotland metres away from curve in road

indicators.note: the metres letter goes away, leaving the word without it

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for metres
camber is the slight arch across a road surface

explanation.surface: A pole in Scotland stands some metres from a bend in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' may suggest a Polish person in Scotland. CAMBER minus M is CABER.
explanation.definitionFit: The caber is the tree-trunk tossed in Scottish Highland Games, a long wooden pole.

clue.text: Jaunt round Llanelli, ignoring the whole centre in port

indicators.note: skipping every middle letter keeps only the two ends of the name

blocks.note: a trip is an outing or jaunt
O is round in shape
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A trip around the Welsh town of Llanelli avoids its town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Llanelli is a town in South Wales; 'round' looks like part of the jaunt but gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya and a seaport on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Problem with cored soft fruit being tough to eat

indicators.note: coring fruit removes its middle, so the central letter goes

blocks.note: as in 'there's the rub'
a berry is a small soft fruit

explanation.surface: A cored piece of soft fruit turns out chewy.
explanation.walkthrough: BERRY loses its middle R to give BERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is rubbery is chewy and elastic, hard to bite through like rubber.

clue.text: Cry in agony with son going after comic books

blocks.note: a yell is a cry
ow is the exclamation of pain
a card is a joker, an amusing person
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A child cries out in pain after another boy grabs his comic books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic books' reads as one phrase; comic is a CARD and books is the definition, in its football sense of a referee booking a player.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee books a player by showing a yellow card, so the cards are the bookings.
